I totally agree w Adam that there’s a lot of shady slop out there marketing tech like NFTs or crypto etc etc, and every new area VCs become obsessed with is framed as the next internet. So it’s good to be SKEPTICAL of any and all marketing. I’m not trying to debunk any of that

In 1999 only 30% of Americans even had a cell phone. So people absolutely did need to be convinced to get on board with the shift. But in terms of AI, I think the corollary is closer to the internet, which also needed a massive campaign to convince people to be ready

The “family plan” was introduced in large part to onboard women and reframe cell phones as an expensive business tool to a family necessity, right when these mom’s teen daughters were also begging for phones thanks to billions of dollars in corporate marketing.

They did this by targeting WOMEN: teen girls and moms. Nokia produced brightly colored phones, phone companies enlisted female celebrities to push their products. Remember the Nokia 8210 Charlie’s Angels collab?! hungermag.com/editorial/noki…

The pricing structure of early cell phone plans reflected their primarily b2b use. When phone companies sought to expand the market in the late 90s/aughts they had to convince moms that the cost was worth it and many moms/women did not see the value at all for such an expense.

This revisionist history is really annoying as someone who’s reported a lot on internet history (buy my book!!). Early cell phones ABSOLUTELY had to be marketed to women, were not quickly adopted by women at all. Cell phones were initially only seen as a tool for execs/sales ppl
